messages:
Zoe (Support): @Emma thanks for filing — quick summary?
Emma (Customer): intermittent crashes when consuming streaming responses in Python SDK json mode. json.loads raises JSONDecodeError.
Zoe (Support): can you paste the minimal repro and the raw bytes that cause it?
Emma (Customer): gist of repro below. using requests.iter_lines() + json.loads. sometimes returns two chunks that split the JSON object.

Emma (Customer): ```py
import requests, json
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json={"mode":"json_stream","prompt":"..."}, stream=True)
for line in r.iter_lines():
    if line:
        print('RAW_CHUNK:', line)
        print(json.loads(line))
```

Emma (Customer): sample raw chunks we captured:
```
b'{"id":1,"text":"Hello'
b' world","more":true}\n'
```

Emma (Customer): so the first chunk ends mid-string and json.loads fails.
Raj (Eng-ML): looks like the SDK/parser is emitting chunks as received instead of buffering until a full JSON object is assembled. Python's json.loads expects complete JSON object, NDJSON assumption needs newline boundaries.
Paul (Eng-SDK): I can repro locally by creating a server that writes partial frames. repro server:

```py
from flask import Flask, Response
import time
app = Flask(__name__)
@app.route('/')
def stream():
    def gen():
        yield b'{"a":1, "text":"part1'
        time.sleep(0.2)
        yield b' part2", "done":true}\n'
    return Response(gen(), mimetype='application/octet-stream')
```

Paul (Eng-SDK): SDK v1.3.0's stream iterator yields each yield() as a chunk and calls json.loads on it immediately.
Raj (Eng-ML): in other languages this shows up differently — TS clients often use TextDecoder and split on "\n"; Go's json.Decoder can decode streams but only if you feed it the combined bytes. The root cause is we removed the internal assembler that concatenated partial frames to avoid latency — but that introduced this bug for non-NDJSON emitters.
Emma (Customer): is there a quick workaround we can use on our side? can't upgrade prod immediately.
Paul (Eng-SDK): workaround: wrap the iterator and buffer until you see a trailing newline or matching braces. naive example:

```py
buffer = b''
for chunk in r.iter_lines():
    buffer += chunk
    if buffer.endswith(b'\n') or buffer.count(b'{')==buffer.count(b'}'):
        obj = json.loads(buffer)
        buffer = b''
```

Paul (Eng-SDK): or switch streaming_mode to "ndjson" on the server side. We'll confirm which models emit NDJSON vs JSON-mode framed output.
Raj (Eng-ML): can you confirm SDK version and a request id? Also we log chunk boundaries in the backend; I'll correlate.
Emma (Customer): SDK 1.3.0, request id req_02a9c4. logs uploaded.
Raj (Eng-ML): thanks. I found the backend trace — we're sending framed JSON objects but sometimes the TCP layer splits them. SDK should handle reassembly. I'll patch.
Paul (Eng-SDK): created PR #542 to restore buffering with a small latency test and a feature flag REDWOOD_STREAM_REASSEMBLE (default on for 1.3.2). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/542 :thumbsup:
Zoe (Support): deploy-bot scheduled rollout of SDK 1.3.2 to edge channel for testing.
deploy-bot: deploy started for package redwood-sdk-python@1.3.2-edge — CI green.
Paul (Eng-SDK): can you test 1.3.2-edge, @Emma? it includes the reassembly fix and a couple tests.
Emma (Customer): installing now in staging...
Emma (Customer): confirmed — staging with 1.3.2-edge no json.loads errors, streaming works. thank you!
Zoe (Support): great — i'll update the ticket and recommend upgrade to 1.3.2. we'll keep the feature flag default-on in GA release.
Paul (Eng-SDK): follow-up action: add explicit tests for chunk-splitting across string boundaries and add a TS/Go compatibility note in docs.
Zoe (Support): closing loop with customer and marking as resolved in support tracker. :white_check_mark:
